instructions:
1. Stand in a split stance, left foot forward, and lean your torso forward to near parallel with the floor.
2. Rest your left hand on your left knee for support and hold a dumbbell in your right hand.
3. Pin your right upper arm against your side, parallel to the floor, with the forearm hanging down.
4. Extend your elbow to drive the dumbbell back until the arm is fully straight.
5. Lower the dumbbell under control to the start. Switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the upper arm fixed and only move the forearm.
2. Move slowly and squeeze the triceps at full extension.
3. Brace your core to stop the torso twisting.
4. Do not swing or use momentum.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand at your side, palm facing in.
2. Place your other hand on your hip.
3. Keep a slight bend in the working elbow.
4. Raise the dumbbell out to the side until the arm is parallel to the floor.
5. Lower under control to the start. Switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with the elbow, not the hand.
2. Keep the torso upright and do not lean toward the weight.
3. Move slowly and avoid swinging.
4. Stop at shoulder height.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand at your hip.
2. Place your other hand on your hip for balance.
3. Keep a slight bend in the working elbow.
4. Sweep the dumbbell up and across your body in a wide arc to chest height.
5. Squeeze the chest at the top, then lower under control. Switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the elbow bend fixed through the arc.
2. Drive the movement from the chest, not the hand.
3. Move slowly and avoid using momentum.
4. Keep the torso upright and core braced.

instructions:
1. Sit at a preacher bench with one arm over the pad, holding a dumbbell in an overhand grip.
2. Press the back of your upper arm into the pad.
3. Curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder by bending the elbow.
4. Squeeze at the top, keeping the wrist firm.
5. Lower under control until the arm is straight. Switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the upper arm flat on the pad to isolate the forearm.
2. Move slowly and avoid using momentum.
3. Keep the wrist locked in the overhand position.
4. Do not let the shoulder lift to help.

instructions:
1. Sit on a bench and rest your forearm on your thigh, palm facing down.
2. Hold a dumbbell in an overhand grip with the wrist past the knee.
3. Let the wrist drop so the dumbbell lowers toward the floor.
4. Raise the dumbbell by extending the wrist as high as possible.
5. Lower under control to the start. Switch arms.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the forearm pinned to the thigh and only move the wrist.
2. Use the full range, down and up.
3. Move slowly and avoid using momentum.
4. Use a lighter weight to keep strict form.
